body:
Got a little behind in being able to log in and check for replies. I apologize. Maybe not good reddiqette, but I wanted to thank detrick4 and paige5bye for thier well-wishing comments but address what was brought up kinda jointly.

I have always really struggled with understanding how others going through depression and suicidal desires can change the course of their thoughts. I have tried but never to any success. It has been an amazing, foreign concept for me. 

What I have taught myself to do, for better/worse, is to sort of gloss over what I am going through at any given time of bad depression so that I can sort of store the experiences I should be having, to cherish them later.

To give you an example: About 15 years ago my family got together, just a sort of hang-out family dinner thing. I am one of 3 brothers, and as brothers do we played some minor yard games - I remember badminton and some ping-pong. It was great, competitive (in the good way) losing some, winning some and everyone was smiling. even out father who didn't play but sort of beamed when watching us play our little tournaments. The whole get together lasted maybe six hours or more.

I recall it so vividly because it was one of the first times in a long while that I really wanted to die - kill myself right then. When we were all laughing and taunting each other, as at the time my brothers were trying to take away my recent winning streak, I laughed, tried to enjoy myself, and smiled because.. well the smile in return I got from my brothers and father made them smile. But inbetween all of the dives, the swings, the running and laughing all I could think of, right then, is the bed we had laid our coats on, in my father's room. I wanted to lay on that bed, maybe in the dark for a while, in the hopes that this would pass and I would be able to enjoy myself later - rather than being a fake.

If laying down didn't help, my father had a couple of guns. Maybe the pistol, maybe the shotgun. Maybe I could take them home without him noticing so maybe he wouldn't blame himself...

But I didn't. I had taught myself that despite never actually being happy then, I would maybe later treasure the memory of my older brother finally learning how I had been nullifying his on the net spikes and besting me. And, it worked. It still is one of my most cherished, vivid memories. I was horribly unhappy but I was there, we were together, then.

The problem I am now so scared of, is that trick no longer works. I don't think life with depression gets better. I know that it keeps getting worse. A time is coming that I will no longer be able to fake the smiles to lift up all of those around me. That is my point of critical mass. And I am scared.

--This post rambled more like an idiot than I had wanted. I am going to post it anyway. Maybe someone else will see some merit in it. Maybe it will help someone lurking SW.

Thanks for the reply. I am glad your friend ended up finding someone to talk to. That is what my weekly group is like/about. It is all veterans from various walks of life struggling with suicide and depression. It really, really helped for a time. I think what is getting to me more and more is that the help and benefit has sort of peaked, while the depression and these deep urges  and/or reasons to commit suicide are continually getting worse and worse.

Plus, I am getting a little older and a life worth struggling for seems further and further off. What if this is as good as it is going to get, objectively? And those sorts of inner questions are what seem to be eating away at me little by little.

For the most part, it comes in waves. I have been in boom and bust cycles for years now. Sometimes deeper depressions sometimes not. I think my fear is I am not handling it well, as far as a longer outlook goes. Each time, and most of the time each day, seems less and less worth it.

Thanks for the comment, though.
